findings.text: 跨Claude/Codex/DSH工作的本地开发者按项目找历史上下文/工具/压缩片段，先用脱敏副本验证，见 [Q01](#research-q01)。
三source装配共享reader生成统一session→UI浏览/快慢搜索，价表解释usage；handoff真实Host命令后读日志观察，管理另写sidecar/删除原日志，见 [Q02](#research-q02)至 [Q06](#research-q06)。
子包/构建alias、Host/Web挂载、三source详情/DSH索引、必要同提交dsh reader入口/usage和kit HTTP、搜索/费用、handoff/brief、删除/metadata、AI/utility关键路径。未执行，未全审三reader归一化/解压/所有UI、Host鉴权/命令或余额凭据。
独立原生Host/Web子包；构建内联同仓shared源码，非整个dsh-plugins集合验收。

#### 依赖

| 条件 | 用途 | 缺失与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DSH>=0.2.1-rc.5 / Node>=24.22.1 | 包声明Host/Web | 未实际安装验收 |
| React19.3.1/Host UI服务 | Web面板/设置 | 不因README证明兼容 |
| 三源根/DSH_HOME/投影 | 读取与观察 | 部分源缺失单独提示 |
| 同提交session-readers/kit | 解析/HTTP/UI基础 | 必要原件绑定、未全算法审计 |
| 本地可信监听/外部认证 | 私密日志访问 | header同源非鉴权 |
| 模型/凭据/Host命令 | AI或handoff可选 | 会外发/执行，首试排除 |

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 资源/现金 | 人工时间 | 边界 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次 | 兼容Host/Node/副本 | profile/源根/隐私配置 | 未测安装时间 |
| 持续 | 扫描/解码/缓存/索引 | 数值/来源核对 | 大日志负担未测 |
| 可选AI/交接 | 模型与工具资源 | 审简报/确认/任务验收 | 不用本地浏览推零费 |
| 失败/退出 | 部分删除/已有目标会话 | 备份与状态核对 | 卸载非任务回滚 |
试用限定独立可信本地Host及脱敏三源副本，只浏览/搜索并核原客户端。不要触删除/改名AI/交接或余额；权限/数值不明就停止回原历史页，见 [Q06](#research-q06)。

#### 效果

| 效果 | 支持 | 未确认 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 跨源找回 | 三入口/项目UI/快慢搜索 | 完整解析/节时 |
| 数值解释 | basis/partial/null | 精确token/实付账单 |
| handoff | create/prompt/日志终态 | 业务完成/持久去重 |
| 会话管理 | sidecar/unlink真实写 | 多文件恢复/可信人批 |
有源隔离、缓存层次、数值依据、交接后观察及删除警告等真实机制；共享helper贡献独立归因，认证/持久幂等/完整解析不在已验范围，见 [Q02](#research-q02)至 [Q06](#research-q06)。
项目轴汇合三源并显式呈现估算/实值与缺口；handoff区分排队、一轮运行和结束，避免只凭prompt接受当成功，见 [Q01](#research-q01)至 [Q04](#research-q04)。
同源header不是鉴权，删除不可逆且多文件可部分成功；handoff内存baseline不耐重启、completed非业务验收，数值/价表不等真账，见 [Q03](#research-q03)至 [Q05](#research-q05)。
未验证方向为持久handoff操作收据与分层验收，先核Host现有去重能力，再以三故障样本测误重试/误成功；已有能力足够则不开发，见 [Q07](#research-q07)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)跨源面板与成熟reader集成novelty25%超单源入口0，未新基础算法不达50%。[Q04](#research-q04)handoff215-349真实投递后读日志改变接受≠完成约束，mechanism50%超25%状态文案；内存baseline/缺持久去重未达75%。[Q02](#research-q02)/[Q03](#research-q03)明确IR精度/来源/失败显示可移植transferability50%超局部25%，多源实际兼容未验不达75%。simplification25%，统一项目入口超0，扫描/管理/交接复杂度没有证实简化50%。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)/[Q04](#research-q04)跨客户端搬运仍同用户审阅与执行，workflow0未改变分工责任，不因少复制升25%。delivery25%，brief141-253将历史线索变成六节可编辑简报并以日志结束区分投递状态，超活动列表0；抽取不保决定真实/任务验收未达50%。reach0，三客户端既有开发者本可打开历史/复制，未见此前受限明确群体，不因统一入口升25%。[Q06](#research-q06)费用可视化/集中浏览不改计费或资源供给服务结构，economics0。

recommendation.reason: 跨 Claude Code、Codex 与 DSH 工作的本地开发者，可在独立 profile 用脱敏日志副本浏览和搜索。它按项目汇合历史，并让上下文数字的来源与交接投递状态更容易核对。无法限制日志访问、解释估算或确认写操作后果时，应停止试用并回原客户端历史页。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)项目跨源回看任务、原各历史页和找回片段结果明确超25%；真实重复摩擦与净效果未测不达75%，取50%。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)三详情与快慢搜索、[Q03](#research-q03)basis/partial和[Q04](#research-q04)投递后状态有可追增量超25%纯入口；reader/任务效果未验不达75%，取50%。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)源到detail/search、[Q04](#research-q04)create/prompt/日志、[Q05](#research-q05)真实删除/门禁支持隔离只浏览试用超25%描述；完整reader/真实Host未验不达75%，源码50%。

cost.rationale: [Q06](#research-q06)Node>=24.22.1/Host版本与源配置、私密日志服务、索引及写/AI排除须主动管理，多项状态退出缺口仍在，取25%；脱敏副本可退超0，未有安装/退出验收不达50%。

      "content": "English | [简体中文](./README.zh.md)\n\n# Sessions Insight · dsh-sessions-insight\n\nA **Sessions Insight** panel for the DSH Web GUI. It parses session logs from **Claude Code, DSH and Codex** and shows what the model actually received on each turn — system prompt, tool definitions, memory & instructions, history, tool results, images — and marks every number as an exact usage figure or a character-based estimate.\n\n![Merged three-source view: workdirs on the left, sessions and turns in the middle, one turn's composition on the right](docs/images/01-merged-tree.png)\n\n> Insight reads never rewrite source logs. Right-click a session and confirm Delete session to permanently remove its original logs.\n\n> **Current scope**: read-only insight, the summary handoff, confirmed deletion, and a settings page with two opt-in utilities (DeepSeek balance and update checks). The handoff delivers a generated brief into a new DSH session and **only calls the official `session.create` / `session.prompt`** — it never hand-writes session events and never rewrites the source session (`docs/HANDOFF.md`, `docs/adr/0003-never-handwrite-session-events.md`, `docs/adr/0007-accepted-is-not-success.md`).\n\n## What it answers\n\n- Of this turn's 392K window, how much is tool schemas, and how much is history?\n- Why does the window jump after turn 7 — where is the compaction point, and what were the sizes before and after?\n- Is 29,018 a usage figure from the log or a chars/token estimate? Every value carries an `exact` / `estimate` badge plus its basis.\n- Across all three sources, how many sessions and turns does a workdir hold, and when was it last touched?\n\n![Turn composition and tool details](docs/images/02-dsh-session.png)\n\n## The interface\n\n**The workdir is the only axis; the source is just a badge.** `workdir → session → turn`\n\n- **Toolbar**: each source's availability and session count (an unreadable source dims, hover for the reason), search, refresh, and a toggle for the project column.\n- **Project tree**: grouped by workdir, with a filter; sessions hang under their project with a source mark, time and file size. The list reads file headers only and parses a session when you open it, so the first open of a big file pays the decode cost.\n- **Session head**: title, source and path, then four stat tiles: current context (share of the window, amber above 80%), peak (and the turn it hit), turns (with compactions and tool calls), and cost.\n- **Turn column**: the \"cumulative level\" chart plots each turn's total context, dashed verticals mark compactions, and clicking a point opens that turn. Below it, one row per turn: the user's words, token count, composition bar, time, tool calls, scaling factor and cost, aligned column by column. Turns load 40 at a time, with \"load more turns\" at the bottom.\n- **Detail column**: \"Turn N\" and the user's words stay pinned at the top; beneath them come the context composition (every part carries an `exact` / `estimate` badge), compactions, tool calls (folded to one-line summaries, failed ones open themselves) and subagent sessions.\n- `⌘K` (`Ctrl+K` on Windows/Linux) opens full-corpus search; a hit jumps straight to that turn.\n\n![Full-corpus search](docs/images/03-search-palette.png)\n\n## Hand off to DSH\n\nOpen a Claude Code or Codex session and click **Hand off to DSH**. Preview and edit the generated brief, confirm the working directory, then click **Deliver to DSH**. The brief has six sections: background and goals, changed files, decisions, open questions and risks, next steps, and verification commands.\n\n![Hand off to DSH: working directory and editable handoff brief](docs/images/04-handoff-dialog.png)\n\n## Settings, balance and update checks\n\nThe settings page is reachable from the **Settings** button in the panel toolbar and from the package details section under DSH settings. It is driven by the Host configuration form; **all six switches are saved by the Host** and the plugin writes no config file:\n\n| Switch | Default | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Session overview | on | Show the Overview tab in the session detail |\n| Skills tab | on | Show the Skills tab |\n| Cumulative level chart | on | Show the context-level chart on the Turns page |\n| Expand tool list by default | off | Open a session with every tool call expanded |\n| DeepSeek balance display | off | Show the balance panel |\n| Automatic version checks | off | Check the registry for a newer package version |\n\n**Both utilities are off by default.** Enabling a switch — or pressing its button — is the only thing that makes the plugin go out. Outbound traffic is limited to two fixed endpoints, `https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance` and `https://registry.npmjs.org/@cyrusdoyle%2F<package>/latest`, with no redirects, no cookies and no caller-controlled URL.\n\n- **Balance** (30 s cache, failures are not cached, an empty wallet list shows as \"no balance\"): follows the credential reference configured for the **DeepSeek official adapter** — its `apiKeyEnv` (default `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) is read from the Host settings service on every request, so renaming it on the Models page takes effect without a restart. When the Host settings service or that entry is missing, or the field is invalid, the lookup silently falls back to the default reference and then to the signed-in DeepSeek account.       "content": "/**\n * HTTP plumbing shared by every route: the same-origin gate, a bounded JSON\n * envelope writer, and query decoding.\n *\n * A route handler owns its response lifecycle — the Host web server does not\n * touch the response after the call — so every branch here writes exactly one\n * and returns.\n *\n * The failure vocabulary is the plugin's, not this module's: a status table is\n * passed in, so `writeFail` maps whatever codes the caller defines without this\n * module importing them.\n *\n * @module @cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugin-kit-host/http\n */\n\nimport type { IncomingHttpHeaders, IncomingMessage, OutgoingHttpHeaders, ServerResponse } from \"node:http\"\n\nimport type { Envelope } from \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugin-kit\"\n\n/** Route handler shape, as the Host web server calls it. */\nexport type RouteHandler = (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse) => void\n\n/**\n * One named route, as `webServer.register` accepts it.\n *\n * A plugin normally registers `exact` paths only: every route is a fixed\n * endpoint, so a prefix mount would hand the same handler arbitrary sub-paths.\n */\nexport interface WebRoute {\n  /** `exact` matches one pathname; `prefix` owns a subtree. */\n  kind: \"exact\" | \"prefix\"\n  /** Pathname, absolute on the site root. */\n  path: string\n  /** Response owner; the server does not touch the response after the call. */\n  handler: RouteHandler\n}\n\n/** HTTP status for each failure code the caller defines. */\nexport type StatusTable<Code extends string> = Readonly<Record<Code, number>>\n\n/**\n * Status one failure code answers with.\n * @param table - the caller's code → status mapping.\n * @param code - a stable failure code.\n * @returns the HTTP status.\n */\nexport function statusOf<Code extends string>(table: StatusTable<Code>, code: Code): number {\n  return table[code]\n}\n\nfunction headerValue(headers: IncomingHttpHeaders, name: keyof IncomingHttpHeaders): string | undefined {\n  const raw = headers[name]\n  return typeof raw === \"string\" ? raw : undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Same-origin gate for a plugin's routes.\n *\n * The check is deliberately conservative and header-only: it refuses a\n * `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` request, and refuses an `Origin` that does not\n * match the `Host` the request was addressed to. A same-origin GET carries no\n * `Origin` at all, so an absent header passes — the gate assumes read-only\n * routes on a listener bound to a concrete loopback address.\n *\n * This is a tripwire, not an authority boundary: a non-browser client can forge\n * both headers. Routes that read user data need a credential check on top.\n * @param req - the incoming request.\n * @returns true when the request may proceed.\n */\nexport function isSameOrigin(req: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  if (headerValue(req.headers, \"sec-fetch-site\") === \"cross-site\") return false\n  const origin = headerValue(req.headers, \"origin\")\n  if (origin === undefined) return true\n  const host = headerValue(req.headers, \"host\")\n  if (host === undefined) return false\n  try {\n    return new URL(origin).host === host\n  } catch {\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Write one JSON response.\n * @param res - the response this handler owns.\n * @param status - HTTP status.\n * @param body - value to serialize.\n * @param headers - extra headers, applied after the defaults.\n */\nexport function writeJson(res: ServerResponse, status: number, body: unknown, headers: OutgoingHttpHeaders = {}): void {\n  const payload = JSON.stringify(body)\n  res.writeHead(status, {\n    \"content-type\": \"application/json; charset=utf-8\",\n    \"content-length\": String(Buffer.byteLength(payload)),\n    \"cache-control\": \"no-store\",\n    \"referrer-policy\": \"no-referrer\",\n    \"x-content-type-options\": \"nosniff\",\n    ...headers,\n  })\n  res.end(payload)\n}\n\n/**\n * Write a success envelope.\n * @param res - the response this handler owns.\n * @param value - payload.\n */\nexport function writeOk<T>(res: ServerResponse, value: T): void {\n  const envelope: Envelope<T> = { ok: true, value }\n  writeJson(res, 200, envelope)\n}\n\n/**\n * Write a failure envelope at the status its code implies.\n * @param res - the response this handler owns.\n * @param table - the caller's code → status mapping.\n * @param code - stable failure code.\n * @param detail - optional specific; never replaces the code.\n * @param headers - extra headers, e.g. `allow`.\n */\nexport function writeFail<Code extends string>(\n  res: ServerResponse,\n  table: StatusTable<Code>,\n  code: Code,\n  detail?: string,\n  headers: OutgoingHttpHeaders = {},\n): void {\n  const envelope = detail === undefined ? { ok: false, error: code } : { ok: false, error: code, detail }\n  writeJson(res, statusOf(table, code), envelope, headers)\n}\n\n/** Largest JSON body any POST route accepts. */\nexport const MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024\n\n/**\n * Read a bounded JSON body.\n * @param req - the incoming request.\n * @param maxBytes - cap; a larger body is dropped rather than buffered.\n * @returns the parsed value, or undefined when the body is empty, too large or malformed.\n */\nexport async function readJsonBody(req: IncomingMessage, maxBytes = MAX_BODY_BYTES): Promise<unknown | undefined> {\n  const chunks: Buffer[] = []\n  let size = 0\n  for await (const chunk of req) {\n    const buffer = chunk as Buffer\n    size += buffer.length\n    if (size > maxBytes) {\n      req.destroy()\n      return undefined\n    }\n    chunks.push(buffer)\n  }\n  const text = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString(\"utf8\")\n  if (text.trim() === \"\") return undefined\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(text) as unknown\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether the request declares a JSON body.\n * @param req - the incoming request.\n */\nexport function isJsonContentType(req: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  const value = headerValue(req.headers, \"content-type\")\n  return value !== undefined && value.toLowerCase().startsWith(\"application/json\")\n}\n\n/**\n * Decode the request URL against a synthetic origin.\n * @param req - the incoming request.\n * @returns the parsed URL; a malformed target degrades to a bare path.\n */\nexport function requestUrl(req: IncomingMessage): URL {\n  try {\n    return new URL(req.url ?? \"/\", \"http://127.0.0.1\")\n  } catch {\n    return new URL(\"http://127.0.0.1/\")\n  }\n}\n\n/** The two refusal codes a method/origin gate answers with. */\nexport interface RefusalCodes<Code extends string> {\n  /** Code for a request that failed the same-origin gate. */\n  forbidden: Code\n  /** Code for a method the route does not serve. */\n  methodNotAllowed: Code\n}\n\n/**\n * Gate every route on origin, then on method.\n * @param req - the incoming request.\n * @param res - the response this handler owns.\n * @param allowed - methods the route serves.\n * @param table - the caller's code → status mapping.\n * @param codes - the caller's refusal codes.\n * @returns true when the caller may continue; a refusal has been written.\n */\nexport function guardRequest<Code extends string>(\n  req: IncomingMessage,\n  res: ServerResponse,\n  allowed: readonly string[],\n  table: StatusTable<Code>,\n  codes: RefusalCodes<Code>,\n): boolean {\n  if (!isSameOrigin(req)) {\n    writeFail(res, table, codes.forbidden, \"origin-mismatch\")\n    return false\n  }\n  const method = req.method ?? \"GET\"\n  if (!allowed.includes(method)) {\n    writeFail(res, table, codes.methodNotAllowed, method, { allow: allowed.join(\", \") })\n    return false\n  }\n  return true\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * One DSH session log assembled into the IR.\n *\n * The job here is *provenance*, not meaning: read the file, split it into its\n * Zstandard frames, parse the lines, find the checkpoint that describes it and\n * decide whether that checkpoint is still current. Everything about what the\n * events mean lives in {@link SessionFold}.\n *\n * A DSH session is a single append-only log of JSON lines split across many\n * frames, plus an optional projection checkpoint the harness folds from it.\n * Everything this adapter knows to be lossy is either normalized (multi-frame\n * decode, turn boundaries, tool pairing, usage arithmetic) or reported in\n * `Session.dataQuality` — never smoothed over.\n *\n * @see docs/PLAN.md (各来源的归一化红线 · DSH)\n * @see docs/IR.md (adapter 必须遵守)\n * @see docs/adr/0004-multiframe-zstd.md\n */\n\nimport { readFileSync } from \"node:fs\"\nimport { homedir } from \"node:os\"\nimport { basename, dirname, join } from \"node:path\"\n\nimport type { Session } from \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-session-contract\"\n\nimport { SessionFold } from \"./fold.ts\"\nimport { decodeSessionLog, splitLogLines } from \"./frames.ts\"\nimport { type DshProjection, isProjectionFresh, type ProjectionAbsence, readProjection } from \"./projection.ts\"\nimport { type LogEvent, parseLogLine } from \"./records.ts\"\nimport { readSessionHeader } from \"./session-meta.ts\"\n\n/** Where DSH keeps its projection checkpoints on this machine. */\nexport const DEFAULT_PROJECTION_ROOT = join(homedir(), \".dsh\", \"storages\", \"session_projcache\", \"sessions\")\n\n/** How well the checkpoint matched the log it was folded from. */\nexport type ProjectionStatus = \"fresh\" | \"stale\" | \"missing\" | \"unreadable\" | \"no-rows\"\n\n/** Everything the probe wants to print that the IR has no field for. */\nexport interface DshReadStats {\n  path: string\n  /** Zstandard frames decoded. */\n  frames: number\n  /** Frames that were found but failed to decode. Must be 0 on a healthy log. */\n  badFrames: number\n  /** True when the final frame was incomplete and was dropped. */\n  tornTail: boolean\n  /** Bytes before the first frame magic. */\n  leadingBytes: number\n  /** JSON lines in the decoded plaintext. */\n  lines: number\n  /** Lines that decoded into an event envelope. */\n  parsed: number\n  /** Lines that did not decode; a non-zero value is a real defect. */\n  invalid: number\n  /** Highest `seq` in the log. */\n  lastLogSeq: number\n  /** Whether the projection could be used. */\n  projectionStatus: ProjectionStatus\n  /** Highest `seq` across the checkpoint's rows, when one was read. */\n  projectionMaxSeq: number\n  /** Per-request records the projection carried. */\n  projectionRequests: number\n  /** Model requests folded into turns. */\n  requests: number\n  /** Tool calls that found their result. */\n  pairedToolCalls: number\n  /** Tool results that named no call of this session. */\n  orphanToolResults: number\n  /** Compaction boundaries found. */\n  compactions: number\n  /** Distinct child sessions linked. */\n  subagentLinks: number\n  /** Turns whose slices came from the harness projection. */\n  projectionTurns: number\n  /** Turns that fell back to character counts. */\n  estimateTurns: number\n  /** Character-scaled turns (always 0 while projections are fresh). */\n  scaledTurns: number\n  /** Turns that kept an explicit `residual`. */\n  residualTurns: number\n  /** Must be 0: negative residual without a structural gap means a broken rule. */\n  overCountedWithoutGap: number\n  /** Projection requests whose category deltas went backwards. */\n  negativeDeltaTurns: number\n  /** Sum of every turn's slices before reconciliation. */\n  rawAttributionTokens: number\n  /** Per-turn raw slice totals, index-aligned with `session.turns`. */\n  rawByTurn: number[]\n  /** Wall-clock milliseconds spent on this file. */\n  elapsedMs: number\n}\n\n/** A parsed session plus the counters behind it. */\nexport interface DshReadResult {\n  session: Session\n  stats: DshReadStats\n}\n\n/** Options for {@link readDshSession}. */\nexport interface DshReadOptions {\n  /** Directory holding `<sessionId>.json` checkpoints. */\n  projectionRoot?: string\n  /**\n   * Pre-read projection, bypassing the disk.\n   *\n   * Tests use this to exercise the fresh and stale paths without writing to\n   * `~/.dsh`, which this plugin never does.\n   */\n  projection?: DshProjection | { absent: ProjectionAbsence }\n}\n\n/** Decode a log and parse its lines, counting everything that did not survive. */\nfunction loadEvents(path: string): {\n  decoded: ReturnType<typeof decodeSessionLog>\n  lines: string[]\n  events: LogEvent[]\n  invalid: number\n} {\n  const decoded = decodeSessionLog(readFileSync(path))\n  const lines = splitLogLines(decoded.text)\n  const events: LogEvent[] = []\n  let invalid = 0\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    const event = parseLogLine(line)\n    if (event === undefined) invalid += 1\n    else events.push(event)\n  }\n  return { decoded, lines, events, invalid }\n}\n\n/** Highest `seq` in one log. */\nfunction lastSeqOf(events: readonly LogEvent[]): number {\n  let lastLogSeq = -1\n  for (const event of events) if (event.seq > lastLogSeq) lastLogSeq = event.seq\n  return lastLogSeq\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve the checkpoint that describes this log, or say why there is none.\n *\n * Freshness decides which basis every turn may use, and a stale checkpoint is\n * discarded whole rather than half-used: its request list would silently drop\n * the newest turns.\n */\nfunction resolveProjection(\n  path: string,\n  sessionId: string | undefined,\n  lastLogSeq: number,\n  options: DshReadOptions,\n): { projection: DshProjection | undefined; status: ProjectionStatus } {\n  const supplied = options.projection\n  if (supplied !== undefined) {\n    if (\"absent\" in supplied) {\n      // A caller that injected an absence means \"pretend the file is not there\".\n      return { projection: undefined, status: supplied.absent === \"missing\" ? \"missing\" : supplied.absent }\n    }\n    return isProjectionFresh(supplied, lastLogSeq)\n      ? { projection: supplied, status: \"fresh\" }\n      : { projection: undefined, status: \"stale\" }\n  }\n  const lookup = readProjection(sessionId ?? basename(dirname(path)), options.projectionRoot ?? DEFAULT_PROJECTION_ROOT)\n  if (lookup.projection === undefined) {\n    return { projection: undefined, status: lookup.absent ?? \"missing\" }\n  }\n  return isProjectionFresh(lookup.projection, lastLogSeq)\n    ? { projection: lookup.projection, status: \"fresh\" }\n    : { projection: undefined, status: \"stale\" }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse one DSH session log into the IR.\n * @param path - a `<cwd bucket>/<sessionId>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd` file.\n * @param options - see {@link DshReadOptions}.\n */\nexport async function readDshSession(path: string, options: DshReadOptions = {}): Promise<DshReadResult> {\n  const started = Date.now()\n  const dataQuality = new Set<string>()\n\n  const { decoded, lines, events, invalid } = loadEvents(path)\n  if (decoded.tornTail) dataQuality.add(\"torn-final-frame-dropped\")\n  if (decoded.badFrames > 0) dataQuality.add(`bad-frames:${decoded.badFrames}`)\n  if (decoded.leadingBytes > 0) dataQuality.add(`bytes-before-first-frame:${decoded.leadingBytes}`)\n  if (invalid > 0) dataQuality.add(`invalid-lines:${invalid}`)\n\n  const header = readSessionHeader(events[0])\n  const headerVersion = header.version\n  if (headerVersion !== undefined && headerVersion !== 4) dataQuality.add(`format-version:${headerVersion}`)\n\n  const lastLogSeq = lastSeqOf(events)\n  const resolved = resolveProjection(path, header.id, lastLogSeq, options)\n  const projectionStatus = resolved.status\n  let projection = resolved.projection\n  const usable = projection !== undefined && projectionStatus === \"fresh\"\n  if (!usable) {\n    if (projectionStatus === \"stale\") dataQuality.add(\"projection-stale\")\n    else dataQuality.add(`projection-${projectionStatus}`)\n    projection = undefined\n  }\n\n  const fold = new SessionFold({ projection, usable, dataQuality, header })\n  fold.fold(events)\n\n  if (!fold.sawTurnEvents) dataQuality.add(\"turn-events-absent\")\n\n  // A turn whose slices could not be measured at all is flagged once here\n  // rather than guessed at inside the attribution.\n  const estimateTurns = fold.window.estimateTurnCount\n  if (estimateTurns > 0 && fold.turns.length > 0) {\n    dataQuality.add(`attribution-estimated-turns:${estimateTurns}`)\n  }\n  if (fold.window.negativeDeltaTurns > 0) {\n    dataQuality.add(`projection-delta-negative:${fold.window.negativeDeltaTurns}`)\n  }\n  if (fold.turns.some((turn) => turn.attribution.residual !== undefined)) dataQuality.add(\"attribution-residual\")\n  // A negative residual means the slices claimed more than the window held; the\n  // rule that forbids it without a structural gap is asserted in the tests.\n  if (fold.turns.some((turn) => (turn.attribution.residual?.tokens ?? 0) < 0)) {\n    dataQuality.add(\"attribution-over-counted\")\n  }\n\n  const session: Session = {\n    id: fold.sessionId ?? basename(dirname(path)),\n    source: \"dsh\",\n    workdir: fold.workdir ?? \"\",\n    createdAt: Number.isFinite(fold.createdAt) ? fold.createdAt : (fold.turns[0]?.startedAt ?? 0),\n    updatedAt: fold.updatedAt === 0 ? (fold.turns.at(-1)?.endedAt ?? 0) : fold.updatedAt,\n    turns: fold.turns,\n    segments: [path],\n    dataQuality: [...dataQuality],\n  }\n  if (fold.title !== undefined) session.title = fold.title\n\n  const stats: DshReadStats = {\n    path,\n    frames: decoded.frames,\n    badFrames: decoded.badFrames,\n    tornTail: decoded.tornTail,\n    leadingBytes: decoded.leadingBytes,\n    lines: lines.length,\n    parsed: events.length,\n    invalid,\n    lastLogSeq,\n    projectionStatus,\n    projectionMaxSeq: projection?.maxSeq ?? -1,\n    projectionRequests: projection?.requests.length ?? 0,\n    requests: fold.requests,\n    pairedToolCalls: fold.ledger.paired,\n    orphanToolResults: fold.ledger.orphans,\n    compactions: fold.compactions,\n    subagentLinks: fold.subagents.size,\n    projectionTurns: fold.window.projectionTurnCount,\n    estimateTurns: fold.window.estimateTurnCount,\n    scaledTurns: fold.window.scaledTurnCount,\n    residualTurns: fold.window.residualTurnCount,\n    overCountedWithoutGap: fold.window.overCountedWithoutGap,\n    negativeDeltaTurns: fold.window.negativeDeltaTurns,\n    rawAttributionTokens: fold.rawAttributionTokens,\n    rawByTurn: fold.rawByTurn,\n    elapsedMs: Date.now() - started,\n  }\n  return { session, stats }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Token accounting for DSH model requests.\n *\n * DSH records four counters per response and one derived total. The recorded\n * arithmetic is `totalTokens = inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens\n * + outputTokens`, and `inputTokens` is the *uncached remainder*, not the whole\n * prompt: once the prefix is cached it falls to a few hundred while\n * `cacheReadTokens` carries the window. The prompt a request actually sent is\n * therefore `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`, which is the same normalization\n * Claude Code needs and the opposite of Codex (where `cached` is already inside\n * `input`).\n *\n * Verified against `contextPressure.pressureTokens`, which the harness derives\n * from the same usage: the two agree exactly on every sampled session.\n */\n\nimport { type JsonObject, numberField, objectField } from \"./records.ts\"\n\n/** One request's token accounting, normalized to this adapter's definition. */\nexport interface DshUsageReading {\n  input: number\n  cacheRead: number\n  cacheWrite: number\n  output: number\n  /** Everything the request sent: `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`. */\n  prompt: number\n  /** The log's own `totalTokens`: prompt plus output. */\n  total: number\n}\n\n/**\n * Read one `assistant/message.data.usage` object.\n * @param usage - the recorded usage object.\n * @returns undefined when the object carries no usable counters.\n */\nexport function readDshUsage(usage: JsonObject | undefined): DshUsageReading | undefined {\n  if (usage === undefined) return undefined\n  const input = numberField(usage, \"inputTokens\") ?? 0\n  const cacheRead = numberField(usage, \"cacheReadTokens\") ?? 0\n  const cacheWrite = numberField(usage, \"cacheWriteTokens\") ?? 0\n  const output = numberField(usage, \"outputTokens\") ?? 0\n  const recorded = numberField(usage, \"totalTokens\")\n  if (input === 0 && cacheRead === 0 && cacheWrite === 0 && output === 0) return undefined\n  const prompt = input + cacheRead + cacheWrite\n  return { input, cacheRead, cacheWrite, output, prompt, total: recorded ?? prompt + output }\n}\n\n/** Read the usage of one `assistant/message` event. */\nexport function readEventUsage(data: JsonObject): DshUsageReading | undefined {\n  return readDshUsage(objectField(data, \"usage\"))\n}\n\n/**\n * Accumulates a turn's requests and watches the recorded arithmetic.\n *\n * Every reading is kept, because a turn's context is the size of its *largest*\n * request while its usage is the sum over requests; conflating the two is how a\n * window gets counted N times.\n */\nexport class DshUsageNormalizer {\n  private input = 0\n  private cacheRead = 0\n  private cacheWrite = 0\n  private output = 0\n  private peak = 0\n  private requests = 0\n  private mismatched = 0\n\n  /** Fold one request into the turn. */\n  observe(reading: DshUsageReading): void {\n    this.input += reading.input\n    this.cacheRead += reading.cacheRead\n    this.cacheWrite += reading.cacheWrite\n    this.output += reading.output\n    this.requests += 1\n    if (reading.prompt > this.peak) this.peak = reading.prompt\n    // The recorded total is prompt + output; a disagreement means the log's own\n    // arithmetic changed and every downstream figure needs re-checking.\n    if (reading.total !== reading.prompt + reading.output) this.mismatched += 1\n  }\n\n       "content": "/**\n * Browser half of the sessions-insight plugin.\n *\n * Contributes one row into the sidebar shell's own global panel list and its\n * page into the layout's keyed `main` slot. The shell then owns the row box,\n * the label, the active highlight and the panel switch exactly as it does for\n * the shipped Plugins and Schedule pages.\n *\n * The two registrations and the locale binding are the kit's; what this module\n * owns is the panel's identity — its id, row order, glyph and page — and the\n * page-lifetime claim that keeps a duplicated injection from mounting twice.\n *\n * Failure policy: nothing here throws out of `apply`. The web shell fails the\n * whole boot when a plugin's apply throws, and an external plugin must not be\n * able to take the GUI down.\n *\n * @module @cyrusdoyle/dsh-sessions-insight/client\n */\n\nimport { registerLocale, registerPanel } from \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugin-kit-client\"\nimport type { ReactElement } from \"react\"\n\nimport { createApi, preloadSessionLists } from \"./api.ts\"\nimport { en, LOCALE_NS, setRuntimeTranslate, t, zh } from \"./locale/index.ts\"\nimport { SettingsStore } from \"./state/settings.ts\"\nimport { UtilityStore } from \"./state/utilities.ts\"\nimport { injectStyles } from \"./styles.ts\"\nimport { ContextInsightPanel } from \"./ui/panel.tsx\"\nimport { registerSettings, type SettingsClientContext } from \"./ui/settings/registration.tsx\"\nimport { makeUtilitySections } from \"./ui/settings/utilities.tsx\"\n\nexport type { ClientContext, Dispose, LocaleFace, SlotsFace } from \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugin-kit-client\"\n\n/** Panel id shared by the sidebar row and the main-slot occupant. */\nexport const PANEL_ID = \"sessions-insight\"\n\n/**\n * Row order among the shell's global panel rows: the shipped Plugins row is 0\n * and Schedule is 10, so this row renders after both.\n */\nconst PANEL_ORDER = 30\n\n/** Services this entry waits for before `apply` runs. */\nexport const inject = [\"slots\", \"locale\", \"uiWorkspace\"] as const\n\ndeclare global {\n  /** Apply guard shared by every module instance in one page lifetime. */\n  var __dshContextInsightApplied: boolean | undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Where the row glyph is resolved from: the shell asks for it at its own size\n * and active state, and this component draws only the glyph.\n * @param props - the shell's icon share: square edge and selection state.\n * @returns the decorative glyph.\n */\nexport function ContextInsightPanelIcon({ size }: { size: number; active: boolean }): ReactElement {\n  return (\n    <svg\n      data-dsh-panel-entry={PANEL_ID}\n      viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\"\n      width={size}\n      height={size}\n      fill=\"none\"\n      stroke=\"currentColor\"\n      strokeLinecap=\"round\"\n      strokeLinejoin=\"round\"\n      aria-hidden=\"true\"\n    >\n      <circle cx=\"6.72\" cy=\"6.72\" r=\"3.92\" strokeWidth={1.12} />\n      <path d=\"M9.6 9.6 13.12 13.12\" strokeWidth={1.28} />\n      <path d=\"M5.12 4.48h3.2\" strokeWidth={1.12} />\n      <path d=\"M5.12 6.72h2.24\" strokeWidth={1.12} />\n      <path d=\"M5.12 8.96h1.28\" strokeWidth={1.12} />\n    </svg>\n  )\n}\n\n/**\n * Mount the browser half.\n * @param ctx - client root context (services: slots, locale).\n */\nexport function apply(ctx: SettingsClientContext): void {\n  // A duplicated client injection (the module factory executed twice in one\n  // page lifetime, e.g. a stale bundle mixed with a rebuilt one) would\n  // otherwise mount a second sidebar row and a second panel page. First\n  // application wins; later calls become no-ops.\n  if (globalThis.__dshContextInsightApplied === true) return\n  globalThis.__dshContextInsightApplied = true\n\n  // Release the claim when this fiber unloads, so a hot-reloaded bundle can\n  // claim again in the same page instead of being silently dropped.\n  if (typeof ctx.effect === \"function\") {\n    ctx.effect(\n      () => () => {\n        globalThis.__dshContextInsightApplied = undefined\n      },\n      \"sessions-insight: apply claim\",\n    )\n  }\n\n  // Styles live in the factory body: the shell tags a factory's side own endpoint handle, so a retry there\n    // does not depend on the panel having mounted first.\n    registerSettings(ctx, settingsStore, utilitySections, createApi())\n  } catch (error) {\n AbortController()\n  const timer = setTimeout(() => {\n    void preloadSessionLists(createApi(), preload.signal).catch(() => undefined)\n  }, 0)\n  ctx.effect?.(\n    () => () => {\n      clearTimeout(timer)\n      preload.abort()\n    },\n    \"sessions-insight: preload lists\",\n  )\n\n  try {\n    registerPanel(ctx, {\n      id: PANEL_ID,\n      order: PANEL_ORDER,\n      locale: settingsSections={utilitySections}\n          onOpenSession={async (id) => {\n            const workspace = ctx.get?.(\"uiWorkspace\") as\n              | { openSession?: (id: string) => void |       "content": "/**\n * Precision made visible.\n *\n * Every number this panel prints is a `Measure`, and a measure that hides its\n * basis is a number pretending to be a fact. These components therefore attach\n * three things to each value: a mark that separates `exact` from `estimate` at\n * a glance, a badge with the same word for screen readers, and a hover/focus\n * tooltip that states the basis and, where the basis is a caliper, its\n * coefficient.\n *\n * The coefficients mirror `src/core/attribution.ts`; they are copied rather\n * than imported so the browser bundle never pulls a module that decodes images\n * with Node's Buffer. `CHAR_CALIBRATION_NOTE` there is the source of truth.\n *\n * @module @cyrusdoyle/dsh-sessions-insight/client/precision\n */\n\nimport type { Basis, Measure } from \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-session-contract\"\nimport type { ReactElement } from \"react\"\n\nimport { t } from \"../../locale/index.ts\"\nimport { formatTokens } from \"../../model/format.ts\"\n\n/** Calipers of the current adapters; see `src/core/attribution.ts`. */\nexport const CALIBRATION = {\n  /** Characters per token for Latin-script text. */\n  text: 2.6,\n  /** Characters per token for CJK text. */\n  cjk: 1.24,\n  /** Characters per token for serialized tool schemas. */\n  schema: 2.26,\n  /** Pixels per token for an image. */\n  pixelsPerToken: 750,\n} as const\n\n/**\n * Human sentence for one basis, used as the tooltip body.\n * @param basis - the measure's basis tag.\n */\nexport function basisTip(basis: Basis): string {\n  switch (basis) {\n    case \"usage\":\n      return t(\"basis.tip.usage\")\n    case \"chars-per-token\":\n      return t(\"basis.tip.chars-per-token\", {\n        text: CALIBRATION.text,\n        cjk: CALIBRATION.cjk,\n        schema: CALIBRATION.schema,\n      })\n    case \"harness-projection\":\n      return t(\"basis.tip.harness-projection\", { px: CALIBRATION.pixelsPerToken })\n    case \"byte-length\":\n      return t(\"basis.tip.byte-length\")\n    case \"unattributed\":\n      return t(\"basis.tip.unattributed\")\n  }\n}\n\n/** The tooltip body for one measure: precision word, basis, calipers, value. */\nexport function measureTip(measure: Measure): string {\n  const precision = measure.precision === \"exact\" ? t(\"precision.exact\") : t(\"precision.estimate\")\n  return `${precision} · ${t(`basis.${measure.basis}`)} — ${basisTip(measure.basis)} (${formatTokens(measure.tokens)} tokens)`\n}\n\n/**\n * Small badge carrying the precision word.\n * @param props - the measure's precision.\n * @returns the badge.\n */\nexport function PrecisionBadge({ precision }: { precision: Measure[\"precision\"] }): ReactElement {\n  // Two literals rather than one interpolated name: Tailwind only sees class\n  // strings that are spelled out in the source.\n  const skin =\n    precision === \"exact\"\n      ? \"px-1 rounded-[3px] font-[inherit] text-[9.5px] leading-[15px] tracking-[0.02em] border-[0.5px] border-current text-ok\"\n      : \"px-1 rounded-[3px] font-[inherit] text-[9.5px] leading-[15px] tracking-[0.02em] border-[0.5px] border-current text-fg-dim\"\n  return (\n    <span className={skin} data-precision={precision}>\n      {precision === \"exact\" ? t(\"precision.exact\") : t(\"precision.estimate\")}\n    </span>\n  )\n}\n\n/**\n * A token count that carries its own provenance.\n * @param props.measure - the measure to print.\n * @param props.share - optional pre-computed share text, e.g. `20.3%`.\n * @param props.dense - drop the visible badge (the mark still separates them).\n * @returns the value with its mark and tooltip.\n */\nexport function MeasureValue({\n  measure,\n  share,\n  dense = false,\n}: {\n  measure: Measure\n  share?: string\n  dense?: boolean\n}): ReactElement {\n  const mark = measure.precision === \"exact\" ? \"=\" : \"≈\"\n  const label = measureTip(measure)\n  return (\n    <span\n      className=\"relative inline-flex items-baseline gap-1 font-mono text-[11px] outline-offset-2\"\n      data-precision={measure.precision}\n      data-tip={label}\n      tabIndex={0}\n      aria-label={label}\n    >\n      <span className={measure.precision === \"exact\" ? \"text-fg\" : \"text-fg-dim italic\"}>\n        {formatTokens(measure.tokens)}\n      </span>\n      <span className=\"text-[10px] text-fg-dim\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n        {mark}\n      </span>\n      {dense ? null : <PrecisionBadge precision={measure.precision} />}\n      {share === undefined ? null : <span className=\"text-[10px] text-fg-dim\">{share}</span>}\n    </span>\n  )\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Handoff: create a DSH session, deliver the brief, and *observe* what happened.\n *\n * The whole state machine exists because prompting a session only proves the\n * content was queued: the model turn starts afterwards, and a model-side failure\n * (a missing credential, for instance) never appears in the call's reply — it\n * lands in the new session's log (docs/adr/0007-accepted-is-not-success.md). So\n * this runner reports \"delivered\" after the queue call and only reports success\n * after it has read a `turn/end` whose reason is exactly `completed`.\n *\n * Two in-process faces are used:\n * - `sessionController.commands` creates the session and queues the prompt. This\n *   is the documented in-process entry (docs/HANDOFF.md): parameter names are\n *   **not** wire-mapped, so there is no `args.request` wrapper here.\n * - the session's own log file is read for observation. The gateway's `follow`\n *   stream is peer-scoped and refuses calls made outside a Remote invocation,\n *   while the log is exactly what the status machine needs.\n *\n * @module @cyrusdoyle/dsh-sessions-insight/host/handoff\n */\n\nimport { stat } from \"node:fs/promises\"\nimport { isAbsolute } from \"node:path\"\n\nimport type { HandoffApplyValue, HandoffStatusValue } from \"../../protocol.ts\"\nimport { isSafeId } from \"../../protocol.ts\"\nimport type { ObservedEvent } from \"../sources/dsh-events.ts\"\nimport { handoffProgress } from \"./progress.ts\"\n\n/** Session creation/queueing, as the in-process controller exposes it. */\nexport interface SessionCommandsFace {\n  /** `sessionController.commands.create`. */\n  create(request: { workspaceId: string; sessionId?: string; agentPreset?: string }): Promise<unknown>\n  /** `sessionController.commands.prompt(request, source)`. */\n  prompt(\n    request: {\n      requestId: string\n      sessionId: string\n      mode: \"queue\"\n      content: { type: \"text\"; text: string }[]\n    },\n    source: { kind: \"user\"; rpcId: string },\n  ): Promise<unknown>\n}\n\n/** A refusal the routes turn into an envelope. */\nexport interface HandoffFailure {\n  ok: false\n  error: \"bad-request\" | \"handoff-unavailable\" | \"not-found\"\n  detail: string\n}\n\n/** What `apply` accepted. */\nexport interface HandoffApplyInput {\n  source: string\n  id: string\n  cwd: string\n  brief: string\n  sessionId?: string\n}\n\n/** Official workspace creation is idempotent by canonical directory path. */\nexport interface WorkspaceCommandsFace {\n  create(request: { path: string }): Promise<{ workspace: { workspaceId: string } }>\n  attach(workspaceId: string, sessionId: string): Promise<void>\n}\n\n/** Everything the runner needs from the Host. */\nexport interface HandoffDeps {\n  workspaces?: WorkspaceCommandsFace\n  /** In-process session commands; absent when the controller is not mounted. */\n  commands?: SessionCommandsFace\n  /** Reads the target session's events; absent means status cannot advance. */\n  observe?: (sessionId: string) => Promise<ObservedEvent[] | undefined>\n  /** Clock override for tests. */\n  now?: () => number\n}\n\n/** Milliseconds a client should wait before polling again. */\nexport const HANDOFF_POLL_MS = 600\n\n/** Characters of brief the runner accepts. */\nexport const HANDOFF_BRIEF_LIMIT = 8_000\n\n/** How many delivered jobs the process remembers. */\nconst JOB_LIMIT = 64\n\n/** Failure codes a log may carry, with what the reader should do about each. */\nconst FAILURE_HINTS: Record<string, string> = {\n  MISSING_CREDENTIAL:\n    \"模型侧没有可用凭证（MISSING_CREDENTIAL）：会话已创建、简报已投递，但模型无法启动。到「设置 → 模型」为当前 provider 添加 API Key 后，在该会话里重发一次即可。\",\n  AUTH_FAILED: \"模型侧鉴权失败（AUTH_FAILED）：检查 API Key 是否有效或是否过期。\",\n  PERMISSION_DENIED: \"模型侧权限被拒（PERMISSION_DENIED）：检查该 provider 的访问权限。\",\n  RATE_LIMITED: \"模型侧限流（RATE_LIMITED）：稍后在该会话重发，简报仍在会话历史里。\",\n  CONTEXT_OVERFLOW: \"上下文超限（CONTEXT_OVERFLOW）：简报对目标模型过长，可缩短后重试。\",\n  TIMEOUT: \"模型侧超时（TIMEOUT）：可稍后在该会话重试。\",\n}\n\nconst FAILURE_CODES = Object.keys(FAILURE_HINTS)\n\nfunction isObject(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {\n  return typeof value === \"object\" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)\n}\n\nfunction messageOf(error: unknown): string {\n  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)\n}\n\n/**\n * Map one command rejection onto our own codes.\n * @param error - whatever the controller threw.\n * @param phase - which call failed, for the detail.\n */\nfunction mapCallError(error: unknown, phase: \"create\" | \"prompt\"): HandoffFailure {\n  const message = messageOf(error)\n  if (message.includes(\"session/not-found\")) return { ok: false, error: \"not-found\", detail: \"session-not-found\" }\n  if (message.includes(\"agent-preset/not-found\"))\n    return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"agent-preset-not-found\" }\n  if (message.includes(\"bad-request\")) return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: `rpc-${phase}-bad-request` }\n  return { ok: false, error: \"handoff-unavailable\", detail: `${phase}: ${message.slice(0, 200)}` }\n}\n\nfunction reasonKind(data: unknown): string | undefined {\n  if (!isObject(data)) return undefined\n  const reason = data[\"reason\"]\n  if (typeof reason === \"string\") return reason\n  if (isObject(reason) && typeof reason[\"kind\"] === \"string\") return reason[\"kind\"]\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/** Message patterns that identify a known failure class, checked in order. */\nconst FAILURE_PATTERNS: { code: string; pattern: RegExp }[] = [\n  { code: \"MISSING_CREDENTIAL\", pattern: /MISSING_CREDENTIAL|no API key|API key for provider|API_KEY (is )?not set/i },\n  { code: \"AUTH_FAILED\", pattern: /AUTH_FAILED|unauthorized|invalid api key|authentication failed|\\b401\\b/i },\n  { code: \"PERMISSION_DENIED\", pattern: /PERMISSION_DENIED|forbidden|\\b403\\b/i },\n  { code: \"RATE_LIMITED\", pattern: /RATE_LIMITED|rate limit|too many requests|\\b429\\b/i },\n  { code: \"CONTEXT_OVERFLOW\", pattern: /CONTEXT_OVERFLOW|context (length|window)|too many tokens/i },\n  { code: \"TIMEOUT\", pattern: /TIMEOUT|timed out|ETIMEDOUT/i },\n]\n\n/** First known failure class mentioned in the attempt records of the window. */\nfunction failureCodeOf(events: readonly ObservedEvent[]): string | undefined {\n  for (const event of events) {\n    if (!event.type.startsWith(\"assistant/\")) continue\n    let serialized: string\n    try {\n      serialized = JSON.stringify(event.data)\n    } catch {\n      continue\n    }\n    for (const code of FAILURE_CODES) {\n      if (serialized.includes(code)) return code\n    }\n    for (const { code, pattern } of FAILURE_PATTERNS) {\n      if (pattern.test(serialized)) return code\n    }\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/** The Host's own failure sentence, for the detail line. */\nfunction failureMessageOf(events: readonly ObservedEvent[]): string | undefined {\n  for (const event of events) {\n    if (!event.type.startsWith(\"assistant/\")) continue\n    let serialized: string\n    try {\n      serialized = JSON.stringify(event.data)\n    } catch {\n      continue\n    }\n    const match = /\"message\":\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.){0,300})\"/.exec(serialized)\n    if (match !== null && match[1] !== undefined) return match[1].replace(/\\\\\"/g, '\"')\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/** Handoff runner. One instance per Host fiber. */\nexport class HandoffRunner {\n  readonly #deps: HandoffDeps\n  /**\n   * Per-session delivery bookkeeping.\n   *\n   * `baselineSeq` is the log's highest `seq` **before** the prompt was sent, so\n   * the observation window is defined by log order rather than by wall clock:\n   * the Host emits `turn/start` as soon as it accepts the prompt, which can be\n   * the same millisecond we record `deliveredAt` — and a short turn wins that\n   * race while a long one loses it and used to stay `delivered` forever.\n   */\n  readonly #jobs = new Map<string, { baselineSeq: number; deliveredAt: number }>()\n\n  /**\n   * @param deps - session commands, log observer and clock.\n   */\n  constructor(deps: HandoffDeps) {\n    this.#deps = deps\n  }\n\n  /** Whether every dependency the runner needs is mounted. */\n  available(): boolean {\n    return this.#deps.commands !== undefined\n  }\n\n  #now(): number {\n    return this.#deps.now === undefined ? Date.now() : this.#deps.now()\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Create the target session and deliver the brief.\n   *\n   * `cwd` is mandatory: omitting it makes the Host inherit its own launch\n   * directory, which silently creates the session under the wrong bucket.\n   * @param input - validated request.\n   * @returns the new session id and the delivered state, or a refusal.\n   */\n  async apply(input: HandoffApplyInput): Promise<{ ok: true; value: HandoffApplyValue } | HandoffFailure> {\n    const commands = this.#deps.commands\n    if (commands === undefined) return { ok: false, error: \"handoff-unavailable\", detail: \"session-controller-missing\" }\n    const cwd = input.cwd.trim()\n    if (cwd === \"\") return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"cwd-required\" }\n    if (!isAbsolute(cwd)) return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"cwd-not-absolute\" }\n    try {\n      const info = await stat(cwd)\n      if (!info.isDirectory()) return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"cwd-not-a-directory\" }\n    } catch {\n      return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"cwd-missing\" }\n    }\n    const brief = input.brief.trim()\n    if (brief === \"\") return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"brief-required\" }\n    if (brief.length > HANDOFF_BRIEF_LIMIT) return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"brief-too-long\" }\n    if (input.sessionId !== undefined && !isSafeId(input.sessionId)) {\n      return { ok: false, error: \"bad-request\", detail: \"invalid-session-id\" }\n    }\n\n    const workspaces = this.#deps.workspaces\n    if (workspaces === undefined)\n      return { ok: false, error: \"handoff-unavailable\", detail: \"workspace-controller-missing\" }\n    let workspaceId: string\n    try {\n      workspaceId = (await workspaces.create({ path: cwd })).workspace.workspaceId\n    } catch (error) {\n      return { ok: false, error: \"handoff-unavailable\", detail: `workspace: ${messageOf(error).slice(0, 200)}` }\n    }\n    let created: unknown\n    try {\n      const request: { workspaceId: string; That is what lets\n * a plugin build inline the internal packages: no build order, no\n * `node_modules` resolution of a workspace link.\n *\n * `tsconfig.json` carries the same mapping as `paths`; TypeScript cannot import\n * this file, so the two are kept in step by hand.\n *\n * @module tooling/aliases\n */\n\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\"\n\n/** Repository root, resolved against this file rather than the caller's cwd. */\nexport const repoRoot: string = fileURLToPath(new URL(\"..\", import.meta.url))\n\n/** Package name → repo-relative path of its TypeScript entry. */\nexport const WORKSPACE_PACKAGES = {\n  \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugin-kit\": \"packages/plugin-kit/src/index.ts\",\n  \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-session-contract\": \"packages/session-contract/src/index.ts\",\n  \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-session-readers\": \"packages/session-readers/src/index.ts\",\n  \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugin-kit-host\": \"packages/plugin-kit-host/src/index.ts\",\n  \"@cyrusdoyle/dsh-plugin-kit-client\": \"packages/plugin-kit-client/src/index.ts\",\n} as const\n\n/** Names of the workspace packages, in dependency order. */\nexport type WorkspacePackage = keyof typeof WORKSPACE_PACKAGES\n\n/**\n * Absolute path of a package's source entry.\n * @param name - a workspace package name.\n * @returns the absolute `src/index.ts` path.\n */\nexport function packageEntry(name: WorkspacePackage): string {\n  return repoRoot + WORKSPACE_PACKAGES[name]\n}\n\n/**\n * The table as tsdown and Vite both spell it.\n * @returns package name → absolute source entry.\n */\nexport function workspaceAlias(): Record<string, string> {\n  const alias: Record<string, string> = {}\n  for (const name of Object.keys(WORKSPACE_PACKAGES) as WorkspacePackage[]) alias[name] = packageEntry(name)\n  return alias\n}\n\n/**\n * The table as Vite/Vitest `resolve.alias` entries.\n * @returns one `{ find, replacement }` per package.\n */\nexport function viteAlias(): { find: string; replacement: string }[] {\n  return Object.entries(workspaceAlias()).map(([find, replacement]) => ({ find, replacement }))\n}\n"
